title: The Detective Memoir of Monkey and Rake
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Inspector Megure, Detective Takagi) omitted by convention; Ran and Sonoko are included as person nodes despite being core cast because they are direct plot participants -- Sonoko is the original theft victim whose stolen bag kicks off the case, and Ran is both the one who recovers the key button evidence and the target of a second attempted murder near the end. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. case_type: attempted_murder (no one dies on-screen). The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep592-593...) actually had the correct culprit (Mizunoe Shinji / s3) and the correct broad mechanic (Masuko was the original Rooster Man, Mizunoe impersonated the persona to stab him) -- unlike several other rebuilds, no culprit correction was needed here. What the old file missed entirely: Sonoko as the original theft victim; Ran being physically attacked a second time by Mizunoe near the dry cleaners (a second attempted-murder beat, resolved by a karate kick Ran learned earlier from Kazumi Tsukamoto in the cold open -- a genuine Chekhov's-gun backstory figure the old file dropped completely); the bankbook/embezzlement blackmail motive (Masuko had been extorting Mizunoe using bankbook evidence of embezzlement, which is Mizunoe's actual motive to kill him); the wet-receipt behavioral clue; the restroom evidence (knife, down jacket, mask) found in the utility closet; and the mechanism by which Ran's picked-up button was later matched to Masuko's own clothing (not Mizunoe's) to prove Masuko was the real Day-1/Day-2 Rooster Man. The old file's single object node 'Rooster costume/button, impersonation clue' has been split into distinct physical objects (mask, knife, jacket, daypack, bankbook, button, receipt) per schema v3's one-node-per-physical-instance rule.
